question_or_symptom: A signal operation can expose a remote value locally before its ACK, completion, tick, or trigger metadata has passed validation.
observation: A complete signal request send followed by timeout, EOF, or a noncanonical response poisons the session, while a canonical non-OK ACK is reusable. After a successful WAIT ACK, timeout or cancellation is retryable without resending. The runtime must stage candidate LOAD/STORE values and publish result fields only after all response and completion checks pass.
conclusion: Signal handles need two distinct commit boundaries: remote indeterminate-ACK poison before acknowledgement and atomic local result publication after complete validation.
decision: Serialize signal calls per instance, form one absolute deadline after argument checks, distinguish pre-ACK poison from post-ACK wait retry, retain accepted waits across local timeout, validate exact identity/predicate/value/tick/correlation, and commit cached value and trigger state only at the final success boundary.
invalidated_assumptions: A timeout is always retryable because signal operations are logically idempotent.
Updating the cached value before validating a successful STORE response cannot leak state after protocol rejection.
